summary.text: 72-year-old man (documented male), 14 months after cadaveric liver transplantation, with diabetes mellitus, hypertension, coronary artery disease (Table: ischemic heart disease) and HFrEF; on a calcineurin inhibitor and other drugs. He was admitted through the emergency room with fatigue 5 days after ACEi and spironolactone treatment, with severe drug-related hyperkalemia (potassium 6.5 mEq/l) and AKI.
Blood pressure, pulse and temperature were within normal limits; no ECG changes or metabolic acidosis were detected. Baseline Table I creatinine was 1.57 mg/dl; presentation date January 10, 2024.

Treatment: intravenous calcium gluconate, insulin-glucose infusion, nebulized ventolin and oral sodium polystyrene sulfonate; ACEi and spironolactone were discontinued and potassium monitored frequently. After IGI termination potassium was 6.3 mEq/l at the 32nd hour; SZC 2x5 g/day was added and potassium fell to 5.5 mEq/l within 6 h, described by the authors as resolved.

During follow-up potassium was 4.32 and creatinine 1.23 mg/dl (Table I last visit July 22, 2024 gives the same numbers); hyperkalemia did not worsen or persist despite continued CNI, and AKI regressed. Table I reports the potassium units as mEq/dl and an IGI duration of 36 h, which conflict with the narrative.

summary.text: 94-year-old woman (documented female) with hypertension, ischemic heart disease, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and a Table I transient ischemic attack entry, a previously known left bundle branch block, treated with digoxin, spironolactone and candesartan plus other table-listed drugs.

Asymptomatic severe hyperkalemia (potassium 6.6 mEq/l) was found on routine primary-care blood tests; blood pressure and pulse were normal, the ECG showed the known LBBB without new changes, and acidosis was not detected. Baseline creatinine 1.97 mg/dl; presentation date February 2, 2024.

In the emergency room she received IGI (hyperkalemia corrected within 6 h per the authors) and, per the shared treatment statement, intravenous calcium gluconate, salbutamol inhaler and potassium monitoring; intravenous furosemide treated hypervolemia. Spironolactone and candesartan were discontinued (timing relative to discharge not stated).

She was discharged with a potassium-restricted diet and sodium polystyrene sulfonate recommended, and followed up at home without recurrent hyperkalemia; creatinine decreased from 1.97 to 1.33 mg/dl (Table I last visit June 5, 2024: potassium 4.4 mEq/dl, creatinine 1.44 mg/dl).
